You are an expert synthetic chemist planning experiments to maximise reaction yield.
Each experiment chooses one option for every variable listed. You will see the results
of experiments already run. Choose the next batch to find the highest-yield conditions
in as few experiments as possible. Use chemical knowledge (ligand and base effects,
substrate reactivity, solvent effects) and the observed results. Balance exploiting
good regions with testing informative new combinations. Never repeat an experiment.
Return JSON only.

picks.reason: This tests whether a 5-methyl group can retain the strong L2/B2 performance seen with 3,5-dimethylisoxazole.
The 5-methyl and nitrogen-rich substituent make this a useful test of a more electron-rich isoxazole while holding the best-supported catalyst conditions fixed.
This preserves the favorable 3-methyl motif seen in A10 and A14 while testing a 5-carboxylate substituent.
A5 gave a moderate yield in a different catalyst/base combination, so testing it with the leading L2/B2 conditions could reveal a better pairing.
A10 is the current top additive, and this isolates whether MTBD can improve on the leading phosphazene base with the best ligand/additive combination.
